item: The law corpus heal re-indexes the article it healed, in the same commit
summary: upsert_law_corpus_article cleared a poll date from published_at (and set the catalog language) on an unchanged-text article and committed, without indexing it again, so every mention kept the poll day in observed_on and the old language: the article sat in one period by its own clock (published_at or created_at) and in another by every reader of the mentions. The heal now goes through the one index_article hook and commits with it (a failed re-index rolls the heal back and the next pass repeats it, where a separate commit would have left nothing to heal); the status stays unchanged and the result says healed and the mention count. A document with nothing to heal is not indexed again. Four tests, three of which fail without the change and one pinning that the steady state pays no extraction; mutants for always-index and commit-first die. Stated limit: the content-changed branch still commits before it indexes, so a failed index there is not repeated (not changed here).
